content.thinking:
I'm planning a chopper motorbike design in Overwatch style, with bold graphite/white/orange blocking and realistic proportions around 2.4m long and 1.1m tall, centered on the Z axis.

I'm sketching the wheelbase and axle placement for a long raked chopper fork, with front and rear wheels at different radii and offsets, then working out the joint hierarchy -- frame root, wheel hinges, steering fork, kickstand -- using hinge-role joints with directional bones.

Now I'm working out how to orient torus geometries so the tires lie correctly along the X axis, defining different tube and radius sizes for the thinner front tire versus the wider rear tire.

I'm planning out the wheel spokes as small radial rods merged or instanced to stay within the triangle budget, and starting to lay out the frame tubes as swept paths with a teardrop-profile tank and custom gradient paint for the orange bodywork with stripe details before moving into the V-twin engine geometry.

Now I'm detailing the engine's crankcase, finned cylinders, chrome header pipes, exhaust routing, seat and fender shaping, ape-hanger handlebars, and lighting elements, settling on an orange accent with graphite and steel tones plus glowing headlight and taillight effects.

I'm working out wheel placement so the tires rest on the ground plane, deciding to model the kickstand retracted while keeping the bike upright, and calculating fork rake geometry from the steering head to the front axle to get a proper chopper-style angle.

Now I'm sketching the frame's joint hierarchy -- steer, front wheel, swingarm pivot, rear wheel, kickstand -- and starting to define the hinge joints with their positions and directions in code.

Still writing helper functions...

Defining the tube sweep helper and wheel-building function, where tires are torus geometries rotated 90° about Y to align their axis with X, with scaling applied to adjust tread width.

Mapping tread blocks around the ring using the u coordinate for alternation, then deciding to skip sidewall pinstriping and instead add separate rim discs for visual detail, positioned at the inner radius of the tire torus.

Still designing the wheel geometry... I'll build the rim as a combination of a torus lip, hub cylinder, brake rotor and caliper, then add six bold box-shaped spokes connecting hub to rim with a center accent disc for style.

Now I'm computing the actual fork and axle geometry — setting front and rear tire widths and thicknesses, then working out the steering head position, triple tree point, and normalized fork direction vector to orient the wheels correctly along the frame.

Mapping out the frame geometry further: top tube running from head tube back through the seat region to rear dropouts, down tube dropping to an engine cradle, and a double-rail cradle loop supporting the engine between the down tube and seat tube.

I'm deciding to make this a hardtail design, dropping the swingarm joint and attaching the rear wheel directly to the root, then laying out the rear rail paths connecting the cradle to the dropouts and widening them slightly to match the rear wheel's width.

Now I'm positioning the top tube curve and placing the engine block with crankcase dimensions near the center, then angling the two V-cylinders off the crank with the front one tilted forward.

Shaping the V-twin cylinders with finned barrel discs, adding valve covers and pushrod tubes, and placing a chrome air cleaner disk on the right side.

Now I'm tracing the exhaust headers from each cylinder's port, curving them down and back along the right side as chrome pipes that merge into a stacked dual-pipe system, while also placing the primary case disc on the left.

For the drivetrain, I'm adding a belt drive on the left side with pulleys at the engine and rear wheel, connected by sweeping rods, then starting to loft the gas tank shape from front to back along the top of the frame.

Shaping the tank as a teardrop with tapered stations from nose to tail, positioning it to sit on the top tube and nestle near the head tube without clipping. Now I'm thinking about the paint scheme—orange base, possibly with flame graphics.

Refining the color boundary calculation...

I'm also thinking about adding a decal emblem on the tank's side—a stylized chevron shape in orange and white, decaled onto the surface with mirrored placement for left/right sides, skipping text/number details since font rendering isn't practical here.

Now I'm positioning the seat loft, working out stations and y-heights so the seat top sits a bit above the top tube.

For the seat material I'm thinking dark brown leather with a diamond stitching pattern, using orange lines across the surface for accent. Next up is the rear fender.

Writing sweep path coordinates...

Now I'm working out the handlebar geometry for ape hangers, calculating the top clamp position off the steering column and building a rising path from the risers up to tall grip height around 1.45-1.5m for that classic chopper silhouette.

I'm placing dark cylindrical grips, brake lever rods, and mirrors, then figuring out the headlight position mounted between the fork tubes near the steering head—checking whether its center at z≈0.93 clashes with the fork tube's raked-back position at that height.

Still working out the headlight assembly, with a forward bucket cylinder, glowing lens disc, and chrome ring torus, plus small bracket rods connecting it to the fork tubes.

Now shifting to the front fender, which needs to arc over the front wheel following the steering geometry — sweeping a thin curved box along points around the axle radius, bone-attached to the fork so it turns with the steering.

Next I'm adding the brake disc, caliper, wheel hub, and axle details on the front wheel, then laying out the spokes radiating from hub to rim on both sides.

Now I'm shaping the tire and rim as torus shapes for both front and rear wheels, with the rear getting a fatter tire and a solid dished disc-style wheel instead of spokes, plus a contrasting ring accent.

I'm designing a reusable spoke-wheel helper function that places rod-shaped spokes radially in the YZ-plane with configurable rim radius, hub radius, spoke count, and thickness, then adding footpegs and forward controls positioned near the lower frame.

For the kickstand I'm figuring out the hinge joint placement near the rear frame rail and its retracted angle, tucking it close to the rail so it clears the rear tire.

For the oil tank and battery box, I'm placing a cylindrical oil tank under the seat on one side, checking its position against the frame rails so it doesn't clip through them, and nudging the x-offset until it clears.

Now I'm adding the darker battery box with cooling slots on the opposite side, then moving on to smaller details: a brake line sweeping from handlebar to caliper, bar-end levers and a small round mirror, a glowing speedo disc on the top clamp, and underglow strips along the frame and engine area.

I'm settling on a single cohesive accent color -- warm orange (#ff8a1e) -- used consistently for glow rim rings, underglow, and other highlights, keeping the white headlight as the only contrast. I'm also planning thin panel line details on the tank and fender, plus tiny merged-sphere rivets for added mechanical texture.

Computing rivet positions along the fender edges...

Estimating total part count around a few hundred, and sketching a compact palette of roughly 14 flat colors plus paint variants — orange, white, graphite, black, steel, chrome, and leather tones.

Writing geometry builder code...

Defining the steering, wheel, and kickstand joints...

I'll skip extra accessory joints like throttle or headlight for now, and start writing a helper function to build box-shaped parts with configurable size, direction, and orientation.

Still figuring out color typing...

Now I'm sketching helper functions: a cylinder builder that supports tapered radii and arbitrary axis direction, a sphere builder for balls, and a rod builder connecting two points with a given radius and sides.

Starting the wheel function...

Still positioning wheel parts...

Still defining spoke geometry and colors, then moving on to building the frame tubes with dark graphite coloring and coordinate paths for the top tube and other frame members...

Still placing frame rails...

Still placing triple trees...

I'm working out the caliper's position relative to the fork slider's angled line, computing z-coordinates at different y-heights to make sure the caliper sits correctly against the rotor without clipping through the slider geometry.

Now I'm setting up the handlebars, sweeping a chrome tube along the steering bone and adding rubber grip cylinders near the end points, using vector interpolation to position the grip rods along the last handlebar segment.

Still placing handlebar details...

Now I'm computing the connecting bracket rods between the fork tubes near the headlight, solving for the intersection point along the fork's slanted axis at y=0.98 so the rod endpoints align correctly with steel material.

For the front fender, I'm setting up an orange box-section arc path in the YZ plane using a parallel-transported frame so the cross-section stays radially oriented as it sweeps over the tire, confirming the default up-vector gives the correct binormal orientation and checking the width against the tire's half-width.

Checking the fender's clearance against the fork at the tightest angle, I found slight overlap and narrowed the half-width to 0.06 to clear it. I'm also considering adding a thin white stripe down the center by painting points near the fender's x=0 plane white.

Now I'm extending that same painted-stripe idea to the rear fender, giving it a wider stripe and dark edges, then checking the rear fender's radius and sweep against the rear tire and frame rails for clearance before setting up struts.

Still working out positions for the fender stay rods connecting the fender to the rail, then moving on to lofting the seat as a bone-frame mesh with painted leather, and starting the tank loft with its own paint color.

I'm adding a chrome tank cap with an orange inner ring positioned at the tank's top curve, skipping the mounting rods and pin striping since paint will cover those details, then planning a decal for the tank badge. For the engine, I'm defining the crankcase as a box sized and positioned beneath the frame cradle, colored with the graphite material.

Next I'm building out the lower oil pan, transmission case, and primary cover with an orange accent ring, then setting up the forward and rear cylinder barrels by computing their directional vectors from the crank center.

Still working out cylinder placement...

Now I'm adding pushrod tubes as chrome rods connecting the case to the head on each side, plus positioning the carb and air cleaner and figuring out exhaust header placement on the front cylinder.

Mapping out the exhaust header paths for both cylinders, tracing each pipe's curve from the cylinder faces down and back toward the rear of the bike.

Keeping it a single pipe on the right side since the pipe at x -0.24 clears the rear tire and cradle fine. Now placing the air cleaner cylinder near the headers, checking it doesn't collide with the rear header position while sitting between front and rear intake runners.

Adjusting belt and pulley positions...

Now I'm placing footpegs and controls, working out rod positions from the body to foot level, sizing peg cylinders with orange rubber grips, and starting on the shift lever geometry.

I'm also figuring out the rear plate placement, calculating the fender end angle to position a white plate box with slight tilt near the tail light area.

Adding a glowing red tail light box, a kickstand rod with a foot pad, and considering orange frame badge accents and small rivet details on the fenders before thinking about underglow lighting.

Now I'm placing thin orange glow rods beneath the crankcase pan on both sides, positioning them carefully to avoid the exhaust pipe geometry, and starting to sketch out a decal SVG with chevron shapes for the tank.

Writing decal SVG...

Now I'm working through the decal placement math — figuring out orientation vectors so the tank graphic displays correctly facing the viewer depending on which side they're looking from.

Adding brake line geometry...

I should skip the throttle cable to save on detail, and I'm checking that the joint helper accepts a role parameter alongside color/fill overloads for rod and sweep calls. Now I'm generating the rivet spheres, placing small sphere geometries at mirrored angular positions around the axle radius on both sides of the wheel.

Writing rivet geometry code...

I'm verifying the geometry fits: the merged rivet mesh gets attached to the frame joint bone, and I'm checking that rivet placement sits just inside the fender's outer radius without poking through, and that the box-section edges clear the rivet positions. I'm also confirming the rear tire's torus dimensions and scaling line up so the wheel sits flush on the ground plane, working out the vertical offset needed so the tire bottom touches y=0 exactly.

I'm checking the front wheel geometry similarly, making sure the torus center height places the tire bottom at the floor, then working out rim radii for front and rear wheels and sketching out the spoke parameters -- count, radius tapering, and position offsets -- for both wheel sizes.

Now I'm adding hub caps, rear brake disc, and axle end caps in steel, defining a wheel-building function signature that takes bone, center, radius, tube radius, width scale, rim/hub radii, spoke count and tapering, then sketching the fork rotor disc dimensions.

I'm deciding to skip the rear rotor since it's mostly hidden inside the tire, and estimating total part counts across frame, wheels, fork, bars, engine, and exhaust to land around 250 pieces total before starting the actual TypeScript build.

Writing engine cylinder geometry...

Adding chrome pushrods between cylinder positions...

Now I'm setting up types for the part options, importing Joint and Fill types, and writing paint functions for the seat stitching pattern and tank finish using conditional color logic based on position and normal direction.
